title: Preemptive egress sluice and soft circuit vent fix
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During a regional egress saturation incident we observed cascading circuit flips that caused noisy failovers and large client tail-latencies. Root cause analysis pointed to two interacting behaviors: (1) the egress admission controller had a single-step deny behavior that produced sudden connection drops under transient overload, and (2) the tenant-level circuit state machine aggressively opened circuits without a graceful vent path for soft shedding, which prevented KV-preserve and warm reconnects.

Goal: Introduce a preemptive egress "sluice" (a graded egress admission path) and a soft circuit vent mode that lets the system shed load in controlled increments while preserving KV cache affinity and providing clearer telemetry for SLO enforcement. This PR contains a targeted hotfix to stabilize regional failover during short surges without changing long-term admission semantics.

What changed (high level):
- runtime/egress_controller.rs: added EgressSluice mode with three internal thresholds (notice/warm-vent/full-deny) and a sliding-window smoothing filter to avoid flip-flopping.
- runtime/circuit_state.rs: implemented "soft_vent" transition which reduces concurrency tokens per-tenant with a probabilistic keep-alive sampler (preserves ~10% KV affinity).
- observability/metrics.go: new metrics (egress_sluice_level, tenant_soft_vent_ratio, sluice_transition_count) and tracing spans for sluice transitions.
- helm/values-operators.yaml: expose sluice config knobs for Dedicated/Private (default off for older clusters).
- tests/load/egress_sluice_integration_test.py: synthetic surge scenarios and KV-affinity assertions.
- docs/reliability/egress-sluice.md: operational runbook with canary instructions and rollback steps.

Implementation notes: The sluice implementation is conservative by default (notice -> warm-vent -> full-deny). We only enable probabilistic soft vent for tenants with >1k TPS historically to avoid impacting small tenants. Thresholds and smoothing windows are tunable via the operator chart; defaults were chosen after three 30m load replay runs.

Testing and verification performed:
- Unit tests: added for state transitions and backoff timers.
- Integration: ran a mixed-traffic surge replay against staging (50k rps sustained for 6 minutes). Observed 62% reduction in abrupt circuit opens and KV-hit retention improved from 23% to 78% for warm vented tenants.
- Chaos tests: simulated region ingress loss while sluice active; service remained responsive with controlled degradation and no global circuit avalanche.
- Load tests: 3x concurrency multiplier with canary 1% -> 10% rollout. Monitoring validated SLO signals remained within soft-warning band rather than hard breach.

Rollback plan: Chart flag toggle (egress.sluice.enabled=false) and circuit_state.soft_vent=false will immediately revert behavior. Runbook includes metric checks to confirm revert (drop of sluice_transition_count to 0, tenant_soft_vent_ratio -> 0).

Operational notes:
- Canary rollout: 1% traffic (stagingset) for 1h, 10% for 2h, full rollout if no regressions.
- Alerting: created temporary PagerDuty policy tied to new metric sluice_transition_rate > 50/min during canary.

Related: ENG-2145 (regional egress hard-deny incidents), SUP-4412 (escalation from customer X during outage).

release_notes: Hotfix: introduce conservative EgressSluice and tenant soft vent to prevent cascading circuit opens during short regional egress surges. Disabled by default for older clusters; operators should follow canary runbook in docs/reliability/egress-sluice.md.
notes_for_ops: Enable via helm flag egress.sluice.enabled=true and monitor observability/egress_sluice_level, tenant_soft_vent_ratio. If short-term regressions appear, toggle flag false and follow runbook rollback steps.
